# RECOUP — Synthesized Go-to-Market & Product Brief

RECOUP is a contingency-priced vendor-spend recovery service (30% of recovered cash / 20% of run-rate avoidance) that statelessly analyzes uploaded contracts, invoices and spreadsheets against 14 forensic rules — auto-renewals, escalators, idle SaaS seats, off-contract rates, duplicates, zombie billing, redundant tools, headcount-fee drift — and hands back a ranked, dollar-quantified findings list plus drafted vendor recovery emails. This brief synthesizes four research streams (product, GTM, PE prospecting, Companies House method) into one operating plan.

## The strategic frame
The recovery-audit industry is real, mature and contingency-priced (PRGX, apexanalytix, CBIZ charge 20–40% of recovered funds) but has historically chased the Fortune 1000 on AP duplicate-payment recovery. RECOUP's wedge is two-fold: (1) the **mid-market** — too small for PRGX to bother with, too lean to have a real procurement function; and (2) a **broader forensic surface** — contract economics (escalators, auto-renewals, idle seats, redundant tools) that AP recovery audits skip. Duplicate/erroneous payments are only 0.8–2% of disbursements; the larger leakage lives in the contract-terms layer RECOUP owns. Companies lose ~9% of revenue to ineffective vendor-contract management.

The single best segment is **PE-backed portfolio companies and roll-ups**. They carry an explicit, time-boxed cost-out mandate (the 100-day value-creation plan), the EBITDA-multiple math makes a recurring £1 of cost worth ~8x at exit (£100k recurring saving ≈ £800k of exit value at the 8.4x median PE multiple), the contingency model fits their cash-constrained/no-upfront-spend posture perfectly, and they are vendor-sprawl machines because they grow by bolt-on acquisitions that bolt on duplicate vendor estates. Best of all the buyer is a channel: win one portfolio CFO and the operating-partner team unlocks 40–160 more companies with the identical problem.

## Product: convert detector into a contingency operating system
RECOUP today is a detector trapped in a browser tab. The three build-now picks — **Recovery Tracker**, **CFO Savings Report**, and **Renewal Calendar** — together convert it into an operating system: the Report wins the deal and justifies the 30% invoice, the Calendar drives the avoidance half of the revenue model, and the Tracker is the system of record that lets you actually invoice 30% of what posts. All three are HIGH feasibility, reuse the existing analysis JSON, and need no database (localStorage + JSON/PDF/CSV/.ics export covers persistence). Strong second tier: a macro SaaS-inflation/CPI benchmark overlay, a clause-matched negotiation playbook library, a what-if savings modeler, and a public ROI calculator for lead-gen (ROI calculators convert >40% vs 2–12% for static pages). Explicitly do NOT build per-SKU price benchmarks, live integrations/continuous monitoring, or a two-way vendor dispute portal — all require persistent state and a data moat that breaks RECOUP's stateless, no-DB design.

## GTM in one line
Sell founder-led, signal-triggered outbound to mid-market CFOs (200–2,000 employees, $5M+ vendor spend, no CPO), anchored on PE operating-partner partnerships as the multiplier channel, with "free unless it lands" as the entire competitive advantage. Lead every message with numbers and timeline hooks (timeline hooks get 10.16% reply vs 4.54% for problem hooks; CFOs reply at 7.59%), one persona per sequence, cohorts ≤50, the free-first-look as the demo.

## Prospecting method
Build the list top-down from Companies House: filter the free monthly Company Data CSV by target SIC codes + MEDIUM/FULL/GROUP account category + `NumMortOutstanding ≥ 1` (leverage signal), join the PSC snapshot to flag controllers named *Topco/Midco/Bidco/Holdings* or a known sponsor, then enrich the shortlist via the free REST API (charges to confirm the LBO debenture, officers for decision-makers, XBRL accounts for admin-expense/headcount). Cross-reference with PE firms' public portfolio pages (LDC ~90 holdings, Inflexion, August Equity, NorthEdge, Endless, Modella) and prioritize fresh carve-outs and active roll-ups, where the cost-out mandate is most acute and contracts are being re-baselined now.

product_opportunities.name: Recovery Tracker — Finding to Posted-Credit board
product_opportunities.what: A client-side kanban/pipeline board moving each finding through the lifecycle every recovery firm uses: Identified -> Email Drafted -> Sent to Vendor -> In Dispute -> Credit Approved -> Posted/Realized (plus Rejected/Won't Pursue). Each card shows dollar value, vendor, rule, drafted email and an evidence checklist; column headers sum dollars so you watch $ identified vs $ realized climb. State persists in localStorage with export/import JSON as the save file.
product_opportunities.why: The single biggest gap between RECOUP-as-detector and RECOUP-as-business. Every contingency firm (PRGX, APEX with 3,000+ active claims, Tangoe) lives on staged claim-status tracking; the market frames credibility as closed-loop tracking from identification through realization with an auditable trail. You cannot invoice 30% of recovered cash without a system of record for what actually posted. Converts a one-time report into a recurring engagement surface.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Pure React state + localStorage, no new data shape — wraps existing findings. Model status, statusHistory[] (timestamp per transition auto-builds the audit trail), realizedAmount, notes per finding. Two headline tiles: Identified $ and Realized $ with a realization-rate % (sells against the 30-60% procurement savings-leakage stat). Wire each card Send button to the existing Gmail draft. Drag-and-drop via @dnd-kit or simple status dropdowns. Add CSV export of the board for the CFO.

product_opportunities.name: CFO Savings Report — downloadable PDF / CSV deliverable
product_opportunities.what: One click generates a branded editorial PDF (plus parallel CSV) the buyer forwards to their CFO: executive summary (total annual savings, recovered cash vs run-rate avoidance, contingency cost, net), findings ranked by dollar with rule + source-clause citation, vendor leaderboard, methodology footer. CSV is the same findings as a finance-importable line-item file.
product_opportunities.why: Every contingency recovery firm's actual deliverable is an audit report detailing findings prioritized by dollar. RECOUP's value is currently trapped in a browser tab the signing CFO never opened. A forwardable artifact closes the deal and justifies the 30% invoice. Lowest-effort, highest-trust output: deterministic, no LLM risk, immediately shareable.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Next.js print-optimized /report route, PDF via browser print pipeline or @react-pdf/renderer / Playwright-to-PDF in a Node route handler — all stateless, fed by existing analysis JSON. CSV trivial via papaparse. Build a print stylesheet matching the ivory/forest editorial design. Include a projected 12-month run-rate avoidance callout and the contingency net math, plus a per-finding evidence appendix pulling the exact contract clause RECOUP already extracts.

product_opportunities.name: Renewal Calendar & Auto-Renewal Watchlist
product_opportunities.what: A timeline/calendar view of every contract's renewal date and notice deadline computed from dates RECOUP already parses. Each item is color-coded by urgency and shows the action window (e.g. 'Notice due by Mar 1 — 60-day window; act by Jan 1 to renegotiate'), with optional .ics / Add-to-Google-Calendar export and a watchlist of the highest-$ upcoming renewals.
product_opportunities.why: Table-stakes across Vendr, Tropic, Sastrify, Zylo, Spendflo. 80% of SaaS contracts auto-renew; negotiating 90+ days out yields ~49% savings vs 19% at 30-90 days; inadvertent renewal is a finding in ~20% of audits. Turns RECOUP forward-looking, which is exactly the run-rate avoidance half of its commercial model. Spendflo's most-praised behavior is flagging renewals 60 days out with benchmark data attached — RECOUP already has both the dates and the benchmark.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Derived view over parsed dates; date math only. noticeDeadline = renewalDate - noticeDays (default 60 if unparsed, flag as assumed). Sort watchlist by annualValue x urgency. .ics generation is a tiny stateless function; calendar push optional via the Google Calendar MCP. Cross-link each renewal to its findings and to the Recovery Tracker so a renewal can spawn a negotiation task. Surface the 'act 90+ days out for ~49% savings' rule as inline coaching.

product_opportunities.name: Benchmark vs SaaS-Inflation / CPI overlay
product_opportunities.what: For each escalator/renewal finding, show the vendor's increase against benchmarks: CPI (~3%), SaaS market inflation (~12-13%), and a fair cap (3-5%, winnable with multi-year commit). Renders a per-finding badge reframing 'you got increased' as 'you got over-increased vs market'.
product_opportunities.why: Benchmarking is the #1 differentiator the leaders sell (Zylo 40M licenses, Tropic Supplier Graph, Vertice $30B index) and the biggest lever in negotiation prep. RECOUP can't match proprietary per-SKU data but can ship public, citable macro benchmarks (Vertice SaaS Inflation Index, BLS CPI) — enough to win the email.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Ship the macro version only: a versioned bundled benchmarks.json (CPI, SaaS inflation, standard caps) with source URLs + comparison math, fed straight into the drafted vendor email as a negotiation anchor. Do NOT attempt per-vendor price benchmarks — that needs a data moat you don't have (LOW feasibility).

product_opportunities.name: Negotiation Playbook Library (clause-matched)
product_opportunities.what: A library of vendor-email/redline templates keyed to each finding type: auto-renewal -> cut notice window to 30 days; escalator -> cap at 3-5% with multi-year commit; idle seats -> true-down language. Each entry carries leverage points and priority order (notice window > price cap > data-export rights).
product_opportunities.why: Upgrades RECOUP from 'one email' to 'a negotiation strategy', matching what Vendr/Spendflo charge for as negotiation-as-a-service. Cheap to build, hard to commoditize content moat.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Static MDX/JSON content mapped to existing rule IDs; deterministic selection, optional LLM personalization, no DB. Each entry: trigger rule, recommended ask, fallback ask, leverage rationale, ready-to-paste redline. Inject the matched playbook into the existing email queue.

product_opportunities.name: What-If / Multi-Scenario Savings Modeler
product_opportunities.what: Dashboard sliders/toggles: realization rate (conservative/base/optimistic), which findings you pursue, escalator-cap assumptions -> recompute total savings and net-after-contingency live.
product_opportunities.why: Mirrors the conservative/base/optimistic toggling buyers expect and makes the savings number feel honest, selling against the 30-60% leakage reality. Good for managing CFO expectations.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Pure client-side recompute over existing findings, no DB. Default base = 60% realization. Pair tightly with the CFO Report (export the chosen scenario) and the Recovery Tracker (scenario = which findings enter the pipeline).

product_opportunities.name: Landing-Page ROI / Savings Calculator (lead-gen)
product_opportunities.what: Public, no-upload estimator: annual SaaS/vendor spend -> estimated recoverable + run-rate avoidance, free unless it lands. 5-8 inputs, branded outcome page, light email gate.
product_opportunities.why: Top-of-funnel growth. ROI calculators convert >40% vs 2-12% for static pages and are perfectly on-brand for a 'free unless savings land' contingency offer. Captures leads before any document is shared.
product_opportunities.buildNotes: Static Next.js page, transparent multipliers from RECOUP's own finding-rate averages (audits typically surface 2-8% of vendor spend), no DB, gate emails to Formspree. Keep ranges honest and conservative to protect credibility into the paid engagement.

gtm.icp: Mid-market companies of 200-2,000 employees / ~$50M-$750M revenue with $5M+ annual third-party vendor + SaaS + services spend and NO dedicated CPO / thin procurement function (70% of SaaS spend is controlled by lines of business, only 26% by IT — decentralized buying is where leakage lives). SaaS alone now runs ~$4,830/employee/yr (+21.9% YoY). Highest-propensity sectors: PE-backed portfolio companies & roll-ups (the single best segment), software/tech-enabled scale-ups, professional services/agencies/staffing, multi-site healthcare/care/vet/dental, manufacturing/distribution/logistics, and multi-location retail/hospitality. Buying-trigger signals: recent PE acquisition or bolt-on, rapid headcount growth (51-53% of SaaS licenses sit unused, 23% never used at all), new CFO/VP Finance just landed, 3+ year-old auto-renewing contracts with 3-7% compounding escalators, recent layoffs leaving idle seats, or a stated cost-cutting mandate. Disqualifiers: <100 employees / <$2M vendor spend (too small to clear a contingency fee), and statutory public-sector procurement where contingency audits face legal limits.
valueProps: Zero-risk, self-funding — free unless we find it. Contingency removes budget approval, RFP and CapEx friction; it is the one audit that never competes for budget. Industry norm 20-40% of recovery, ROI routinely >300%, clients recover 2-4% of audited spend on average (10-20% on specific supplier relationships).

Found money plus locked-in run-rate avoidance, in dollars, fast — RECOUP sells a ranked dollar-quantified findings list AND drafted vendor emails (recovery is teed up, not just diagnosed). Companies lose ~9% of revenue to vendor-contract mismanagement; one documented missed renewal locked in $183.6K of overpayment on idle seats for 12 months.

Forensic breadth beyond what a recovery auditor or your own team checks — 14 rules across auto-renewals, off-contract rates, idle seats, escalators, duplicates, zombie billing, redundant tools and headcount-fee drift. Legacy firms mostly hunt duplicate payments (only 0.8-2% of disbursements); RECOUP owns the bigger contract-economics layer they skip.

No lift on your team, no rip-and-replace — stateless analysis of uploaded PDFs/Excel/Word, no DB, no integration project, no IT ticket. Removes the #1 mid-market objection (we don't have the bandwidth).
Speed + privacy — stateless means nothing stored, fast turnaround, easy to clear with legal/security vs a 6-12 week enterprise recovery engagement.

For PE: a recurring pound of cost removed is worth ~8x at exit (8.4x median PE EBITDA multiple), reframing the 30%/20% contingency fee as trivially cheap against enterprise-value uplift — the single most powerful close in the PE world.
channels: Founder-led / rep-led signal-triggered outbound (email + LinkedIn as one multi-touch motion) — the primary channel. CFOs reply at 7.59% to good cold email; finance engages with numbers and timeline hooks. Own this.

PE / VC portfolio partnerships — sell once to a sponsor's value-creation/operating-partner team, get warm intros to 10-40 portfolio CFOs with a built-in margin mandate. Highest-leverage channel for the roll-up ICP; a single contingency case study per fund unlocks the portfolio.

Referral + revenue-share with adjacent advisors — fractional CFOs, outsourced controllers, FP&A consultancies, M&A integration/QoE firms, RevOps/IT-asset-management consultants. They sit on the exact triggers (new finance leader, post-merger) and 'free unless we find it' is easy to forward with zero downside.

Free analysis as the demo — because the product is stateless document analysis, the offer IS the proof. Lead magnet: send one vendor contract + 12 months of that vendor's invoices, we show what we'd recover, free. Collapses the sales cycle.
Targeted founder-led content + peer benchmarks on LinkedIn (not a blog farm) — 'we analyzed N mid-market vendor stacks, here's the average leakage.' Supports outbound; not standalone.

Niche communities/events — fractional-CFO networks, regional PE associations, procurement meetups. Trust-building, not volume. De-prioritize paid search/display (intent thin, dominated by PRGX/Apex SEO), cold calling, and generic webinars.

objections.objection: We don't have budget for this.
objections.rebuttal: There's nothing to budget. We're contingency — you pay only a share of cash we actually recover or run-rate we avoid. If we find nothing, you owe nothing. It's the one audit that never competes with your budget. Contingency self-funds; ROI routinely exceeds 300%.

objections.objection: Our finance/AP team or internal audit already checks this.
objections.rebuttal: They check that invoices match POs — duplicate-payment hygiene, ~1-2% of spend. We work the contract-economics layer they don't have time for: compounding escalators, auto-renewal windows, idle seats, redundant tools. Even tight AP teams have 0.8-2% slipping through, and the contract leakage is bigger. If your team's already perfect, our audit finds zero and costs you zero — a clean bill of health for free.

objections.objection: We already use PRGX / a recovery auditor.
objections.rebuttal: Great — they're excellent at duplicate payments, freight and rebates. We're complementary: we cover SaaS seats, contract escalators, auto-renewals and redundant tools — the categories an AP recovery audit doesn't touch. Different rules, no overlap, same contingency model.

objections.objection: I don't want to damage vendor relationships.
objections.rebuttal: We draft every vendor email for you and you control what gets sent — nothing goes out without your sign-off. Overcharges are almost always honest errors; a reputable vendor returns them and the relationship stays intact. A vendor-sensitive approach is how the whole recovery-audit industry operates.

objections.objection: We don't have the bandwidth / it's a big project.
objections.rebuttal: Zero integration, no IT ticket, no rip-and-replace. You upload vendor PDFs, Excel and Word — we do the forensics statelessly and hand you a ranked, dollar-quantified list. Minimal internal effort is the whole point.

objections.objection: Is our data safe? These are sensitive contracts.
objections.rebuttal: Stateless by design — we analyze the documents and store nothing in a database. Easy to clear with your security and legal teams; no data-retention exposure.

objections.objection: How do I know the savings are real / that you won't inflate findings?
objections.rebuttal: Every finding is ranked in dollars and traced to the exact clause and invoice line that proves it — you see the source document. Our fee is only on cash you actually recover or run-rate you actually avoid, so we have zero incentive to inflate; phantom savings pay us nothing.

30% of money you'd otherwise never see — the other 70% is pure margin you weren't going to have. Compare that to a fixed consulting fee paid whether they find anything or not. And it's only 20% on avoidance, where the recovery is forward-looking. For a PE-backed business, a recurring saving is worth ~8x at exit, so the fee is trivial against enterprise value.

companies_house:
Companies House gives RECOUP a free, top-down way to build a PE-backed mid-market prospect list. The free REST API base URL is https://api.company-information.service.gov.uk (register on the Developer Hub, mint an API key, authenticate via HTTP Basic with the key as username and a blank password). Rate limit: 600 requests per rolling 5-minute window (~2 req/sec sustained; 429 on overage).

KEY ENDPOINTS: GET /advanced-search/companies is the workhorse for ICP filtering (params: company_name_includes/excludes, company_status, company_type/subtype, sic_codes (comma-delimited), incorporated_from/to, location, size, start_index). GET /company/{number} returns status, sic_codes, accounts (category + dates), date_of_creation. GET /company/{number}/persons-with-significant-control surfaces ownership (the PE structure). GET /company/{number}/charges reveals debentures/mortgages (the LBO leverage signal). GET /company/{number}/officers maps decision-makers, and GET /officers/{id}/appointments finds serial PE operating-partner directors across a portfolio. Note: advanced search does NOT filter on account category, charges or PSC directly — filter by SIC + status, then enrich each hit with the profile/charges/PSC calls.

BULK PRODUCTS (for scale): The free monthly Company Data Product CSV (download.companieshouse.gov.uk/en_output.html, all ~5M live companies) is the primary sieve — columns CompanyName, CompanyNumber, CompanyCategory, CompanyStatus, IncorporationDate, RegAddress.* (geo), SICCode.SicText_1..4 (sector), Accounts.AccountCategory (size proxy: FULL/GROUP/MEDIUM/SMALL/MICRO/DORMANT), Mortgages.NumMortOutstanding (leverage), and PreviousName_1..10 (rebrands follow buyouts). The PSC Data Product (full-register JSON snapshot) is joined to find PE-controlled companies. The free Accounts Data Product (iXBRL, ~75% of filers) is parsed for turnover, headcount and administrative expenses — the line RECOUP's savings live in.

PE/SIZE FILTERS: (Signal A, strongest) PSC/RLE naming the PE corporate stack — Topco -> Midco -> Bidco, with a Relevant Legal Entity holding >75%; regex PSC names for \b(TOPCO|MIDCO|BIDCO|HOLDCO)\b plus INVESTMENTS/CAPITAL/PARTNERS/FUND/LP/SARL or Jersey/Guernsey/Cayman registration, or a known sponsor name. Always walk UP from the opco to the group/holdco to see the fund (the opco PSC may list individuals). Verified example: Pagabo Group Limited (13306964) PSC = 'Th 55 Group (Midco) Limited', 75%+ — 'Midco' is the tell. (Signal B) Charges/mortgages = LBO debt registered against Bidco/Midco; NumMortOutstanding>0 + recent incorporation + holdco-style name is the buyout fingerprint, confirmed via /charges (all-assets debenture to a bank/credit fund). (Signal C) Size: target Accounts.AccountCategory of MEDIUM/FULL/GROUP (~£10M-£150M turnover, up to ~250-employee 'medium' through lower-large; exclude MICRO/DORMANT). UK thresholds from 6 Apr 2025: Medium = turnover <=£54M, balance sheet <=£27M, <=250 employees. (Signal D) SIC codes for vendor-heavy sectors: 62012/62020/62090 IT & software consultancy, 58290 software publishing, 82990/70229 business support/consultancy, 64999/66190/66300 financial & fund services, 86900/87300 healthcare/care, 78200/78300 staffing, 52290/49410 logistics.

RECIPE: (1) Company Data CSV -> keep CompanyStatus=Active AND SICCode in target list AND AccountCategory in {MEDIUM,FULL,GROUP} AND NumMortOutstanding>=1. (2) Join PSC snapshot -> keep rows whose top RLE matches Topco/Midco/Bidco/Holdings or a known sponsor -> flag 'PE-backed'. (3) API-enrich shortlist via /charges (confirm LBO debenture), /officers (decision-makers), /filing-history (recent refinance), XBRL accounts (admin-expense/headcount). (4) Rank by estimated recoverable vendor spend; feed to the 14-rule engine and email drafter.
